messages.subject: Answer: Distance stratification problem
parts:
Hi Luis,

You're not the first person to ask me about this, so I'm replying to the
distance-sampling list as well as to you.

The symptom of your problem is that whenever you try an analysis with
stratification the distance analysis engine returns the message:

** Warning: Area of each stratum has not been defined or is zero. Distance
cannot produce an abundance estimate (but will still calculate density). **

In your case, this is occuring because you changed the name of the stratum
data layer from the default "Region" to "Survey". Nothing wrong with doing
this - in fact its a good idea to give the data layers sensible names rather
than using the defaults. However, its easiest to do this before you start
defining and running analyses. This is because when you change the stratum
name, Distance isn't smart enough to update the stratum definition section of
the model definitions you have already created. So, to fix your problem you
just need to edit all the model definitions you have created that include
stratification and, on the estimate tab, under "Use stratum layer:" click on
the new stratum name in the drop down box.

In general, I'd recommend making all changes to your dataset *before* you
start defining and running analyses.

Note that your problem has nothing to do with the fact that you imported the
data, or that you subsiquently typed in the areas.

Another general point: thanks for sending me a project file demonstrating
your problem - this made it very easy to see the source and recommend a
solution. However, if you (or anyone else!) wants to send project files in
future can you please compress them (e.g., in a zip file) first! Too many
half-megabyte email messages will give our mail server a headache. Thanks.

All the best,

- Len Thomas


On Mon, 30 Aug 1999 19:40:34 -0400, Continental Shelf Associates, Inc. wrote:

> >Len,
> >
> >Help! I was wondering if you could help me with a problem when I was running
> >Distance 3.5 release 4.
> >
> >I'm working on aerial survey data for marine mammals off the Chesapeake Bay
> >area and in this particular case/problem, bottlenose dolphins. I've
> >attached the Distance project that I had a problem with. I imported the
> >data from Quattro as a comma delimited file using the Import Wizard but
> >forgot to include a column for the stratum area. After the import was
> >complete, the stratum area had 1 in all records. I edited the field/column
> >by typing in the area (7050) for each stratum. The first run without
> >stratification went fine and gave density and abundance estimates. The
> >second run with stratification returned an error saying that the startum
> >area was not defined or equal to zero. I don't know what's wrong or why
> >Distance would make an abundance calculation for one set and not for
> >another. Do I have too many fields?
> >
> >Hope you could clear this up without too muich trouble on your part. Thank
> >you for whatever assistance you can give.
> >
> >Luis Lagera Jr.
